subject: Re: Finalizing post-close orchestration & canary schedule for RiverMark
summary: Mutual action plan attached with a three-phased post-signature orchestration: low-traffic canary, staged migration, and end-user training. Includes success criteria, rollback triggers, and required RiverMark deliverables (SSO certs, test dataset).
messages:
From: Claire Adams <claire.adams@rivermarkhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@rivermarkhealth.com>, impl-team@rivermarkhealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-close orchestration items (MAP + canary windows)

Tessa —

Thanks again for a smooth procurement process. Legal finished redlines yesterday and we’ve countersigned; finance will push the first invoice early next week. Before we lock dates on our side I want to confirm a concrete post-close plan so we can align internal stakeholders (security, SRE, training).

High level asks from RiverMark:
- A clear MAP with owners and due dates (SSO certs, IP allowlist, test data)
- A canary window that doesn’t affect live patient workflows (we want lightweight traffic slices)
- Training for two cohorts (ops + clinical) with recorded sessions

We’ve attached a one-page internal checklist — would you confirm Redwood’s proposed windows and any blockers you see? Prefer to have canary start no earlier than June 7, ideally week of June 14.

Claire Adams
Program Director, Digital Ops
RiverMark Health

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Claire Adams <claire.adams@rivermarkhealth.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-close orchestration items (MAP + canary windows)

Claire —

Congrats on getting the contract signed, and thanks for the clear checklist. I’ve attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (Rivermark_MAP_v1.0.pdf) that embeds the post-signature orchestration you asked for. Key points up front:

- Canary timing: we propose a 3-week staged canary starting the week of 2027-06-14. Week 1: 10% production traffic (read-only flows), Week 2: 30% (mix of read/write with rate limits), Week 3: 60% with throttles in place; full cutover targeted 2027-07-05.
- Migration approach: incremental sync of historical embeddings, KV cache warm-up, and database read routing for two weeks before write cutover. We’ll do a dry run of the sync on 2027-06-02 against anonymized test data.
- Training: two 90-minute cohort sessions (Ops: 2027-06-21, Clinical: 2027-06-23) plus on-demand recordings and a sand-box for testers.
- Success criteria / rollback: latency < 350ms p50 for MAP traffic, error rate < 0.5% during canary. Any sustained spike above thresholds for more than 10 minutes triggers automatic rollback to the previous model variant and an incident call.

Action items I need from RiverMark to lock dates:
1) SSO cert and IdP test account (due 2027-06-03)
2) IP allowlist entries for our dedicated egress (see SAML_config_template.txt)
3) 2-3 representative PII-scrubbed test queries for validation (due 2027-05-31)

Vivek, Marcus — can you confirm the runbook items in Canary_Runbook_RiverMark.xlsx align with our autoscale and KV-warm policies? Grace — please draft the training invite and share sign-up links by Monday.

I’ll schedule a 30-min MAP review with Claire + RiverMark stakeholders next Tuesday (2027-05-25) to finalize dates and owners.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Rivermark_MAP_v1.0.pdf, Canary_Runbook_RiverMark.xlsx, SAML_config_template.txt

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-close orchestration items (MAP + canary windows)

Quick alignment on infra details —

I reviewed the runbook. A few notes:
- Autoscale: we’ll provision a dedicated 2-GPU canary pool (pinned instance type) for the first two weeks then scale to 4-GPU on week 3 if metrics look good. That keeps unit cost predictable.
- KV cache warm-up: prefer a staged pre-warm step 48 hours before canary start to pre-populate hot prefixes; we’ll use synthetic traffic so no PHI leaves RiverMark systems.
- Model fallback: we’ll keep a smaller 7B variant available for automatic fallback (in case of GPU OOM or perf regression). Fallback is transparent via routing policy and will be exercised in the dry run on 2027-06-02.
- Observability: need RiverMark to enable access for two read-only accounts so our logs/traces can be pushed to their Splunk instance (instructions in the runbook).

If all good I’ll add these items to the MAP with owners and post the updated runbook in Drive. Marcus, confirm target memory/seq-length assumptions so I can size the pool.

— Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Claire Adams <claire.adams@rivermarkhealth.com>, Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@rivermarkhealth.com>, impl-team@rivermarkhealth.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-close orchestration items (MAP + canary windows)

Claire / Elliot —

Thanks for the productive MAP review earlier today. Per our discussion, I’m confirming the finalized owners and dates below (also pushed the updated MAP to Drive). Please review and ACK by EOD Thursday so we can lock the canary pool.

1) Deliverables (RiverMark)\- SSO cert + IdP test account — Claire (due 2027-06-03)
- IP allowlist (squad network) — Elliot (due 2027-06-03)
- Test dataset (PII-scrubbed) — impl-team (due 2027-05-31)

2) Redwood deliverables\- Dry-run sync & fallback test — Vivek (run 2027-06-02)
- Canary deployment & monitoring — Marcus (start 2027-06-14)
- Training invites & recordings — Grace (sessions 2027-06-21 and 2027-06-23)

3) Canary schedule (final)
- 2027-06-14 to 2027-06-20: Week 1 — 10% traffic (read-only)
- 2027-06-21 to 2027-06-27: Week 2 — 30% traffic (limited write flows, rate-limited)
- 2027-06-28 to 2027-07-04: Week 3 — 60% traffic (scale-up if metrics stable)
- Full cutover target: 2027-07-05 (final decision on 2027-07-02 after SRE review)

4) Success criteria / Rollback triggers\- Latency p50 < 350ms; p95 < 700ms for canary traffic
- Error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m => auto-fallback + incident call
- Any security incident or failed SSO test => pause and remediate before proceeding

5) Communication cadence\- Daily canary standups (10am PT) during canary weeks
- Post-canary retrospective and lessons learned (2027-07-07)

Attachments and links: I’ve reattached the MAP and runbook; SAML template and DocuSign envelope are in the Drive folder.

Next step: Claire, once you ACK the owners/dates we’ll send a calendar hold for the dry run and training invites.

— Tessa
Senior Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Rivermark_MAP_v1.0.pdf, Canary_Runbook_RiverMark.xlsx, SAML_config_template.txt
